Highly motivated and self-driven with a focus on successfully delivering results for the team and meeting overall company goals. Demonstrated capacity acting as a resource for colleagues with less experience
Extremely organized and detail-oriented with the ability to manage large amounts of data from various inputs and consolidate the information for critical business decisions (data analytics).
Strong interpersonal, persuasion, influencing and collaboration skills required, working to build consensus. Ability to explain difficult or sensitive information in a cohesive and digestible way to broad audiences.
Demonstrates flexibility and the ability to multi-task and balance competing priorities constantly and meet strict deadlines.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to anticipate and identify issues or barriers and generate solutions, using a high level of personal discretion in decision-making.
Demonstrates in-depth understanding of supply chain operations and financial acumen, with knowledge and proficiency across multiple supply chain functions, enabling effective coordination and communication across competing demands.
Solves complex problems; takes a new perspective on existing solutions; exercises judgment based on the analysis of multiple sources of information.
Agility to work within broad guidelines and policies to impact a range of customer, operational, project, or service activities within own team and other related teams.
Knowledge of best practices and how own area integrates with others; is aware of the competition and the factors that differentiate them in the market

Qualifications

7-10 years of experience of supply chain, demand planning, purchasing, inventory control and /or supplier management.
Strong working proficiency with Microsoft Office, including expert-level functionality with Excel.
Minimum 3 years’ experience working with SAP S4/HANA and analytical software (PowerBI, Tableau, SAP Analytics Cloud, etc.).
Knowledge of project management application tools and best practices.
Strong written and oral presentation skills.
Experience working with diverse, cross-functional teams.

Technical knowledge of operational and manufacturing processes (design, assembly, integration, and test)

new_jobs.description:
About Agile Defense

At Agile Defense we know that action defines the outcome and new challenges require new solutions. That’s why we always look to the future and embrace change with an unmovable spirit and the courage to build for what comes next.

Our vision is to bring adaptive innovation to support our nation's most important missions through the seamless integration of advanced technologies, elite minds, and unparalleled agility—leveraging a foundation of speed, flexibility, and ingenuity to strengthen and protect our nation’s vital interests.

Title: Program Managers, Deputy Program Managers, Senior Project Managers & Project Managers (CBP) 

Clearance: Active CBP Background Investigation (CBP BI) and EOD strongly preferred. We can begin processing for candidates who do not hold one.

Citizenship: U.S. Citizenship required Location: [required] | [on-site / hybrid posture required]

Salary Range: [required]

Signing Bonus: $10,000 for candidates with an active CBP BI. Payable after 90 days; standard terms apply.

Travel: occassional as needed

The Work
U.S. Customs and Border Protection runs continuous operations across more than 300 land, air, and sea ports of entry, plus Border Patrol stations and the Air and Marine Operations Center. Delivering technical work into that environment is a different problem from delivering it into an office. You cannot take a checkpoint down on a Tuesday because the schedule says so. Change windows are narrow, some sites are hours from the nearest support, and a slipped date can mean an officer working without a tool they were told to expect.

We are hiring project and program managers to run delivery across that constraint. You will coordinate work spanning network, cloud, cybersecurity, and field deployment teams, manage commitments with the customer, and move work through federal change control and accreditation processes that set the pace whether or not your plan accounted for them.

One thing is worth knowing before you apply. This is not a role where the schedule is the job. The engineers here can build; what slows delivery is dependency, approval, access, and the gap between what a plan assumed about a site and what is true at that site. Managers who treat those as somebody else's problem do not do well here.

What Success Looks Like
Objective 1: Turn commitments into schedules that survive contact with a 24/7 environment

Plans account for the change windows and site access constraints that actually govern the work, not the ones that are convenient to plan around

Dependencies between network, cloud, security, and field teams surface before they become a delay

Estimates come from the people doing the work, and get challenged rather than either accepted whole or overwritten

When a date moves, the customer hears it from you, with a reason and an option

Objective 2: Give the customer a picture of the program that matches what is happening

Status reporting tells the customer something they can act on rather than a color that covers a problem

Risks appear on the register while there is still time to do something about them

The customer stops arranging side conversations to find out how the work is really going

What you report measures delivery rather than activity

Objective 3: Remove the obstacles that keep engineers from delivering

Blockers get resolved at the lowest level that can resolve them, and escalate quickly when they cannot

Engineers spend their time on the work instead of chasing approvals, access, and equipment

Recurring administrative friction gets fixed at its source rather than absorbed again every month

Where You'd Fit
We are hiring across several levels, and one of these roles is scoped by portfolio rather than by seniority. You do not need to pick one before applying. Tell us where you think you land and we will talk about it.

Project Manager. You own a project's scope, schedule, and delivery. You make routine sequencing and resourcing calls yourself and bring the ones with customer impact to a review

Cloud Project Manager. You own delivery of the cloud workstream, including its dependencies on security and accreditation. You decide sequencing across builds, migrations, and authorization milestones

Senior Project Manager. You take the projects that arrive without a clear path, including the ones already in trouble when you get them. Other project managers check their approach with you before committing to a date

Deputy Program Manager. You own a defined slice of the program full time and step into the Program Manager's authority when they are unavailable. Escalations that would otherwise reach the Program Manager come to you first, and most stop there

Program Manager. You own whether the program delivers as a whole, including commitments you inherited and work you do not directly manage. You are the customer's counterpart when something goes wrong

What You Bring
Minimum Qualifications

[Verbatim from the labor category, per level. These differ across Project Manager through Program Manager, including Deputy Program Manager. Note: a prior Agile Defense Deputy Program Manager performance profile exists and should be used as the baseline for that rung's qualifications and objectives once available, rather than drafted fresh. State the band honestly rather than publishing the highest bar. Required before publishing.]

Preferred Experience

You have delivered technical work in a federal program where change control and accreditation set the pace

You have told a customer bad news early, and can describe how that conversation went and what it cost you

You have run delivery across teams you did not manage and had no authority over

You have taken over a project that was already behind and can say what you changed first

You hold an active CBP BI, a fitness determination at another DHS component, or an active DoD clearance. Any of these shortens your start date

You know enough about infrastructure, cloud, or security work to challenge an estimate without needing someone to translate it for you

PMP, agile delivery certifications, or equivalent are useful, but they are not a substitute for having delivered

A note on timing
We are staffing this program now. If you already hold an active CBP BI and EOD, your start date is short and a $10,000 signing bonus comes with the role, payable after 90 days under standard terms. We would like to talk this week.

If you do not, we can begin processing a CBP BI for you. That takes months rather than weeks, so applying now means joining a pipeline rather than starting immediately. We would rather tell you that up front than have you find out after you apply.

Employee Benefits
Agile's benefits offerings include, dependent upon position, Health Insurance, Life Insurance, Paid Time Off, Holiday Pay, short-term and long-term Disability, Retirement and Learning and Development opportunities as well as other optional benefit elections.

Our Core Values

Employees of Agile Defense are our number one priority, and the importance we place on our culture here is fundamental. Our culture is alive and evolving, but it always stays true to its roots. Here, you are valued as a family member, and we believe that we can accomplish great things together. Agile Defense has been highly successful in the past few years due to our employees and the culture we create together. 

What makes us Agile? We call it the 6Hs, the values that define our culture and guide everything we do. Together, these values infuse vibrancy, integrity, and a tireless work ethic into advancing the most important national security and critical civilian missions. It's how we show up every day. It's who we are.

Happy
- Be Infectious. Happiness multiplies and creates a positive and connected environment where motivation and satisfaction have an outsized effect on everything we do.

Helpful
 - Be Supportive. Being helpful is the foundation of teamwork, resulting in a supportive atmosphere where collaboration flourishes, and collective success is celebrated.

Honest
 - Be Trustworthy. Honesty serves as our compass, ensuring transparent communication and ethical conduct, essential to who we are and the complex domains we support.

Humble
 - Be Grounded. Success is not achieved alone, humility ensures a culture of mutual respect, encouraging open communication, and a willingness to learn from one another and take on any task.

Hungry 
- Be Eager. Our hunger for excellence drives an insatiable appetite for innovation and continuous improvement, propelling us forward in the face of new and unprecedented challenges.

Hustle
 - Be Driven. Hustle is reflected in our relentless work ethic, where we are each committed to going above and beyond to advance the mission and achieve success.

About BAE Systems Electronic Systems

BAE Systems, Inc. is the U.S. subsidiary of BAE Systems plc, an international defense, aerospace and security company which delivers a full range of products and services for air, land and naval forces, as well as advanced electronics, security, information technology solutions and customer support services. Improving the future and protecting lives is an ambitious mission, but it’s what we do at BAE Systems. Think Consulting is seeking a Sr. Project Manager for our client, who in under two years has stood up a modern cloud data platform, launched a new enterprise data and analytics environment, implemented a corporate financial planning system, kicked off an enterprise CRM selection, and begun consolidating multiple ERP environments. This is a hands-on delivery role, not an administrative one: you will personally run the largest, most cross-functional IT programs — ERP consolidation, CRM implementation, data platform build-out, integration and AI initiatives — while establishing the project management standards, intake process, and reporting cadence a growing IT function needs. Success means delivered outcomes and credible commitments: sponsors who know what they're getting and when, and project teams that are never surprised.

Key Responsibilities

Project & Program Delivery

Own end-to-end delivery of assigned enterprise IT projects and programs — charter, scope, schedule, budget, resourcing, risk, change control, testing, cutover, and post-go-live stabilization.
Serve as lead project manager on the highest-complexity initiatives in the portfolio, including ERP consolidation workstreams, the enterprise CRM implementation, data platform and integration build-out, and infrastructure or M&A integration projects.
Build and maintain realistic integrated schedules that reflect operating company availability, seasonal field workload, and fiscal-year and month-end constraints — not idealized plans.
Run disciplined risk and issue management with named owners, escalation thresholds, and decision logs; escalate early rather than absorbing slippage silently.
Own project financials — estimate to complete, forecast versus approved budget, capital versus expense treatment, and vendor invoice validation against milestones.
Drive user acceptance testing, training, cutover, and adoption planning with the business, treating change management as part of delivery rather than an afterthought.
Manage post-acquisition IT integration projects as the organization continues to acquire, including system rationalization, user onboarding, and data migration.

PMO Practice & Governance

Establish and operate the IT project intake, prioritization, and demand management process so the portfolio is sequenced against capacity rather than by whoever asks loudest.
Define and maintain the project management standards for IT — lifecycle stage gates, templates, estimating norms, RAID discipline, status reporting, and closeout criteria — sized to a lean function, not a bureaucracy.
Produce executive-level portfolio reporting for the VP of Information Technology and business leadership: status, milestones, spend, risks, and dependencies across the portfolio in one consistent view.
Maintain the cross-project dependency map — the ERP, CRM, data platform, and integration programs share the same people, systems, and cutover windows.
Mentor project coordinators, analysts, and IT leads who run smaller efforts, raising delivery consistency across the department.
Contribute to annual IT planning, capital request preparation, and multi-year roadmap sequencing.

Data & Integration Projects

Lead projects that depend on data as the deliverable, not just the byproduct — reporting migrations, master data cleanup, data warehouse build-out, and analytics rollouts.
Plan and manage data migration and data conversion workstreams across multiple ERP environments, including extract, cleanse, map, load, and reconciliation cycles with business sign-off at each stage.
Partner with the data and integration teams to schedule integration platform work, retire point-to-point integration debt, and sequence API-based patterns alongside application projects.
Build data quality, master data, and reconciliation acceptance criteria into project plans so systems go live on trusted data — one customer definition, one work order process, one employee record.
Coordinate reporting and analytics deliverables with the data team so business users have reporting ready at go-live, not months after.
Ensure projects produce the documentation, lineage, and access controls needed to withstand sponsor and transaction diligence.

AI & Emerging Technology

Manage delivery of AI initiatives across the portfolio — enterprise AI assistant rollout and adoption, document and submittal automation, field and service workflow assistants, estimating and takeoff support tools, and AI-assisted reporting.
Run AI use case intake and evaluation with a consistent framework: business problem, data readiness, expected benefit, risk, cost to run, and how success will be measured — so pilots are chosen deliberately rather than by vendor pitch.
Insist on the prerequisites before AI projects start — governed data, documented lineage, defined access controls, and a named business owner — coordinating with the data and cybersecurity functions.
Manage responsible-use guardrails in partnership with cybersecurity, legal, and HR: acceptable use, data residency and confidentiality, customer and employee data handling, and human review of AI output where it touches contracts, safety, or pricing.
Drive AI projects past the pilot stage into measured production adoption, including training, workflow redesign, and benefit tracking; recommend shutting down pilots that do not earn their keep.
Track the AI capabilities arriving natively in the ERP, CRM, EPM, and productivity stack, and sequence them into the roadmap rather than building custom equivalents.

Stakeholder & Vendor Management

Act as the primary delivery contact for business sponsors across Our Client's operating companies — finance, operations, service, preconstruction, HR, and field leadership.
Manage implementation partners, systems integrators, and software vendors against statements of work, milestones, deliverable quality, and knowledge transfer commitments.
Negotiate and control scope with vendors and sponsors alike, and hold partners accountable to committed timelines without damaging the relationship.
Translate between technical teams and non-technical stakeholders, including field and shop personnel who will use the systems.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in information systems, computer science, engineering, construction management, business, or equivalent practical experience.
7+ years managing enterprise IT or technology-enabled business projects, including at least 3 years leading programs with multiple concurrent workstreams and a seven-figure combined budget.
Demonstrated ownership of at least one full-lifecycle enterprise application implementation — ERP, CRM, HRIS, EPM, or comparable — from selection or planning through go-live and stabilization.
Working command of both traditional and iterative delivery methods, and the judgment to apply the right one; comfort operating without a large PMO behind you.
Practical experience managing data migration, integration, or reporting workstreams, including reconciliation and business sign-off.
Command of project financials — budgeting, forecasting, estimate to complete, and vendor milestone validation.
Track record managing implementation partners and software vendors against contracted scope and deliverables.
Ability to hold a credible delivery conversation with a CFO and a field superintendent on the same day.
Willingness to travel across operating company and project locations as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in construction, MEP, specialty trades, industrial services, or another project-based, field-heavy business.
Experience in a multi-operating-company or acquisitive environment, including post-acquisition system and data integration.
Direct experience on an ERP consolidation or multi-ERP rationalization program.
Experience delivering AI or automation projects into production — enterprise AI assistants, document automation, or workflow assistants — including adoption and benefit measurement.
Familiarity with a modern cloud data and productivity stack and with an iPaaS platform.
Experience standing up project intake, prioritization, or portfolio reporting where little process previously existed.
PMP, PgMP, PMI-ACP, Certified ScrumMaster, or Prosci change management certification.
Experience with field technology — mobile service, dispatch, timekeeping, or project management platforms used in the trades.

We didn’t just build a layer on top of old tech; we built America’s most private and secure mobile carrier from the ground up. By building our own network from scratch, we are able to design and build a suite of privacy and security features that no other carrier on the planet can offer.

Skylo has pioneered a standards-based approach to satellite connectivity. We connect smartphones and IoT devices directly to satellites. No special hardware, no entirely new networks. Just billions of existing devices, suddenly reachable anywhere on Earth. We're not building toward this future. We're already in it.

Our direct-to-device service is live on millions of activated devices across five continents, covering more than 72 million square kilometers, in partnership with leading satellite operators, mobile network operators, Tier-1 chipset makers, and OEMs worldwide. And we're just getting started.

At the heart of it all is Skylo's commercial NTN vRAN: a 3GPP standards-based, cloud-native platform that seamlessly bridges terrestrial and satellite networks. It's the infrastructure that makes true anywhere, anytime connectivity possible.

When you join Skylo, you'll work at the intersection of three markets reshaping how the world stays connected: mass-market consumer devices, automotive, and industrial IoT. Enabling people outdoors and critical workflows in the world's most remote places.

This is a rare chance to work on technology that matters, at a company that's already proving it works

This role is located in Mountain View, CA where we are onsite 3 days a week.

How You Will Impact Skylo

This role will own one of the broadest execution surfaces at Skylo. You'll own the primary execution bridge across Software Engineering, Network Engineering, Product, Product Support and Customer Success, on infrastructure that has to hold across satellite operators, carriers, chipset makers, and OEMs on five continents.

As Director of Program Management, you'll build and lead the team that turns that breadth into predictable delivery, organized as two pods: Technical Program Management as the integration layer, and Program Operations as the operating backbone. Your job is to make deployment at this scale predictable and customer-focused, and to build a team that sustains a culture of invention while operating a global network at scale.

In this role, you will

Lead a team across Technical Program Management and Program Operations that leaders across the company trust to deliver.
Own technical program execution across Software Engineering, Network Engineering, Product, Product Support, and Customer Success, so complex programs ship integrated rather than in pieces.
Manage inter-team dependencies, surface risk early, and clear blockers before they stall delivery.
Apply engineering judgment to trade-offs between speed, performance, and technical debt, and catch risks before they reach a customer.
Establish the processes, tooling, and delivery standards the rest of the org relies on to ship predictably as scope and headcount grow.
Run the operating rhythms that turn strategy into commitments the company hits: quarterly planning, mid-quarter reviews, retrospectives, and feedback loops.
Shorten the loop from field issue to engineering fix, building the feedback channels from customer operations into core engineering that harden the system with every release.
Give leadership and external partners a reliable view of status, trade-offs, and risks they can plan against.

You might thrive in this role if you

Have built and scaled technical program management teams inside complex software, networking, or telecom environments.
Lead well without direct authority. You align multidisciplinary teams through influence, clarity, and credibility rather than reporting lines.
Are technically fluent in cloud-native architectures, network engineering, and global carrier operations.
Have partnered directly with enterprise customer TPM leadership to run joint programs.
Follow through on what you commit to, and communicate technical status honestly, including to executives and external partners.
Are deeply curious and quick to learn. You dig into unfamiliar domains, ask the questions others skip, and welcome feedback and mentorship.
Do your best work in a fast-paced, high-growth company. You're comfortable building a structure where little exists yet, then reshaping it as the company scales.

new_jobs.title: Technical Project Manager III
new_jobs.description:
Firefly Aerospace is a space and defense technology company on a mission to reliably and repeatedly launch, land, and operate space systems from Earth to the Moon and beyond. As the partner of choice for critical space missions, Firefly is the first
commercial company to launch a satellite to orbit with 24-hour notice and the first
company to achieve a successful Moon landing. Headquartered in north Austin, Texas, Firefly is looking for passionate, hardworking innovators to join our team and help fuel our successful trajectory into space.

Summary

As a Technical Project Manager in Firefly’s Electrical Engineering department, you will own the planning, scheduling, and execution rhythm for avionics development across all of Firefly’s product lines. You will report to the Director of Electrical Engineering and serve as the programmatic arm of the department, covering Hardware, Firmware, Harnessing, Launch Vehicle Systems, and Spacecraft Systems.

This is a hands-on role. You will build and maintain the integrated schedules the Director owns, keep department development programs and IRAD efforts visible, and make sure avionics commitments to vehicle programs are real, tracked, and closed. You will work directly with electrical engineering leads and subject matter experts to translate technical input into executable plans and maintain the documentation and risk posture needed for program success.

Responsibilities

Build and maintain integrated schedules for avionics development, spanning all vehicle-level programs and internal IRAD.
Manage schedules, backlogs, and risks for avionics teams across Hardware, Firmware, Harnessing, Launch Vehicle Systems, and Spacecraft Systems.
Support the Director in staffing and resource planning by maintaining a clear picture of department capacity against program demand.
Track progress on the common modular architecture effort, including reuse commitments across launch vehicles and spacecraft.
Maintain schedules covering System Requirements Reviews (SRR), Preliminary Design Reviews (PDR), Critical Design Reviews (CDR), qualification and acceptance test campaigns, and flight readiness milestones.
Tie avionics delivery dates to board bring-up, harness availability, and integration and test bench readiness so plans reflect real hardware constraints.
Interface with vehicle Program Management to surface programmatic and technical issues early and drive them to resolution.
Support department budget tracking and electrical engineering cost reduction projects with schedule and data analysis.
Support documentation preparation for design reviews and program gates, aggregating inputs from engineers and functional leads.
Track and manage department risks, mitigation plans, and action items to closure.
Maintain and automate program metrics dashboards using Python or SQL for data extraction and reporting.
Facilitate sprint planning, stand-ups, and retrospectives for avionics teams using Agile or hybrid workflows.
Maintain project information and visibility using the Atlassian Suite (Jira, Confluence).
Support proposal inputs and cost estimating for avionics scope as needed.

Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor’s degree in a technical field such as engineering, computer science, or similar.
5+ years of experience in technical project management or program integration for complex engineering systems.
Demonstrated success building and maintaining integrated schedules for hardware or embedded development in a fast-paced environment.
Aerospace or space systems experience, particularly in avionics, electrical systems, or spacecraft operations.
Proficiency with Atlassian tools: Jira (issue tracking, dashboards, reports) and Confluence (documentation, templates, macros).
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail in maintaining schedules, risks, and review materials.
Basic proficiency in Python and SQL for data analysis, automation, or reporting.
Excellent written and oral communication skills, capable of distilling technical details into clear, actionable plans.
Proven ability to collaborate across multiple engineering disciplines and with internal customers including Program Management, IT, Supply Chain, and Manufacturing.

Desired

Experience managing schedules through qualification and acceptance test campaigns.
Experience managing development in a hardware-constrained environment where delivery depends on board, bench, or vehicle availability.
Familiarity with system-level design reviews and program lifecycle processes.
Experience integrating Agile practices within a systems engineering or hardware-centric organization.
Understanding of configuration management, documentation control, and technical baseline maintenance.
Exposure to proposal writing, cost estimating, or budget tracking.
Working knowledge of embedded software, real-time operating systems, or hardware-in-the-loop test environments.

Mission

As a Program Manager, you will lead the Service Profitability and Continuous Product Improvement (CPI) programs, reporting to the Head of Program Management in Proton Therapy R&D.

The role is responsible for turning service and product improvement needs into a coherent portfolio of initiatives that maximizes customer value, operational performance, and business impact while ensuring alignment across Product Management, Service, Regulatory and R&D.

The first program, Service Profitability, is a strategic program aiming at adapting the way our Proton Therapy centers operate and improve reliability and stability of our system. The program takes place in a context of large growth of the installed base ; has large strategic impact directly impacting IBA’s P&L ; is monitored at executive level ; and is already on-going with multiple product developments within R&D and non-product projects coordinated with Service.

The Program Manager will establish and operate the governance framework, perform value-based prioritization, ensure stakeholders alignment (service, product management, component managers etc.), facilitate stewardship principle in an Agile context and provide visibility on the overall improvement portfolio and its return on investment.

The position provides executive leadership and strategic direction for staff supporting personnel security, industrial security, information security, classification, badging, foreign ownership and facility clearance programs, security surveys, and program support functions.
The Program Manager ensures contract performance complies with DOE directives, federal regulations, security policies, quality standards, and performance objectives while maintaining close coordination with federal leadership, site offices, laboratories, contractors, and stakeholders across the DOE Office of Science enterprise.
Major Duties and Responsibilities:

Program Leadership and Contract Management:

Serve as the primary interface between the Contractor and DOE Contracting Officer's Representative (COR), Contracting Officer (CO), and federal program leadership.
Provide executive direction, supervision, and management of all task areas performed under the contract.
Ensure seamless integration of personnel, processes, systems, and services across multiple locations and organizational elements.
Establish performance objectives, priorities, schedules, and resource requirements to support mission execution.
Monitor contract execution and ensure all deliverables are completed accurately and on schedule.
Lead transition, startup, and continuity-of-operations activities.
Coordinate with DOE organizations, M&O contractors, laboratories, and external stakeholders regarding security support services.

Personnel Management:

Recruit, assign, supervise, develop, and retain qualified security professionals.
Ensure staffing levels support mission requirements and contract performance standards.
Conduct performance management, workforce planning, succession planning, and employee development activities.
Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, professionalism, and customer service.
Ensure personnel maintain required qualifications, certifications, training, and security clearances.
Authorize and oversee employee professional development programs consistent with DOE requirements.

Strategic Security Program Oversight:

Provide executive oversight and integration of:
Personnel Security Programs
National Security Clearance Processing
HSPD-12 and Credentialing Programs
Human Reliability Program (HRP)
Classification and Declassification Programs
Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) Programs
Information Security Programs
Industrial Security Programs
Facility Clearance (FCL) Programs
Foreign Ownership, Control, or Influence (FOCI) Programs
Safeguards and Security Survey Programs
Badging and Access Control Operations
Classified Visits and Assignments
COMSEC, OPSEC, TSCM, and Technical Security Programs
Workplace Substance Abuse Program Support
Security Metrics, Analytics, and Reporting Activities

Quality Assurance and Performance Management:

Develop, implement, and maintain the contract Quality Control Program (QCP).
Monitor service delivery, performance metrics, staffing effectiveness, and customer satisfaction.
Conduct internal reviews, audits, and corrective action activities.
Ensure continuous process improvement and operational excellence.
Identify performance risks and implement mitigation strategies.
Support DOE reviews, assessments, surveys, and inspections.

Budget and Business Operations:

Prepare budget forecasts, staffing projections, and resource plans.
Monitor labor utilization, costs, and financial performance.
Support DOE planning, programming, budgeting, and evaluation initiatives.
Analyze contract trends and make recommendations for improved efficiency and effectiveness.
Provide annual budget information and support financial reporting requirements.

Reporting and Communications:

Prepare executive briefings, performance reports, management summaries, and status updates.
Ensure submission of bi-weekly activity reports and ad hoc reports required by the Government.
Present performance metrics, program status, risks, and improvement initiatives to federal leadership.
Maintain effective communication with all stakeholders regarding contract execution and operational issues.

Safety and Compliance:

Ensure integration of safety into all management and operational activities.
Maintain compliance with DOE Orders, federal regulations, local procedures, and applicable laws.
Promote a safe and secure workplace environment.
Ensure protection of classified information, controlled information, personnel data, and government assets.

Minimum Required Qualifications

Education:

·Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in one of the following fields: Security Management, Criminal Justice, Business Administration, Public Administration, Emergency Management, Intelligence Studies, Information Assurance, Homeland Security, or related discipline.
·Master's degree preferred.
Experience:

Minimum 10 years of progressive experience managing federal security, safeguards, industrial security, personnel security, or national security programs.
Minimum 5 years of experience managing large, complex federal contracts and multidisciplinary teams.
Experience supporting DOE, DOD, DHS, Intelligence Community, or other federal national security organizations.
Demonstrated experience managing security operations involving classified information, personnel security, industrial security, and physical security programs.
Experience overseeing geographically dispersed personnel and multiple task areas.

Security Clearance:

Active DOE Q Clearance or Top Secret clearance with the ability to obtain and maintain all required DOE access authorizations.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Extensive knowledge of DOE Safeguards and Security requirements.
Knowledge of DOE Orders 470 Series, 472 Series, 473 Series, 475 Series, and related federal security regulations.
Knowledge of Trusted Workforce 2.0 initiatives and personnel vetting requirements.
Strong leadership, organizational, and strategic planning skills.
Exceptional written and oral communication abilities.
Experience with performance metrics, dashboards, and data analytics.
Ability to manage complex stakeholder relationships.
Strong risk management and problem-solving capabilities.
Ability to lead multidisciplinary teams in high-security environments.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Power BI, and related business systems.

Desired Certifications:

Project Management Professional (PMP)
Certified Protection Professional (CPP)
Industrial Security Professional (ISP®)
Security Fundamentals Professional Certification (SFPC)
Program Management Certification
DOE National Training Center security certifications relevant to assigned responsibilities.

Supervisory Responsibility:

The Program Manager has full authority and responsibility for all contractor personnel assigned under the Technical Security Support Services contract and is accountable for contract performance, staffing, quality control, budget execution, and customer satisfaction across OSS, CSC, and OREM mission areas.
This position is designated as Key Personnel and requires DOE review and approval before assignment or replacement.
Position Contingency:

This position is contingent upon successful award of the Office of Science contract and completion of all required background investigations, site access approvals, and onboarding requirements. Employment offers, start dates, and continued employment are dependent upon successful contract award.

At Boeing, we innovate and collaborate to make the world a better place. We’re committed to fostering an environment for every teammate that’s welcoming, respectful and inclusive, with great opportunity for professional growth. Find your future with us.

Join our dynamic Security team and help protect our organization from evolving threats. We are seeking a Threat Intelligence Analyst with expertise in investigative analysis, threat intelligence, digital forensic, security monitoring, and risk mitigation. Your work will directly support our Insider Threat Program, cybersecurity program, and broader information security initiatives, helping safeguard critical assets and ensure compliance with security best practices. Help protect classified information systems and sensitive organizational data from internal and external threats.

Key Responsibilities:

Use intelligence aggregation tools to review and assess potential insider threats.
Monitor for concerning behaviors and escalate high-risk incidents for investigation.
Conduct investigative activities including forensic acquisition and analysis of digital assets, interview planning, gathering statements, and resolving allegations.
Recover stolen intellectual property and perform forensic analysis of systems or malware as required.
Produce clear, detailed reports documenting investigative findings, outcomes, and security incidents.
Partner with Security, HR, Legal, and other stakeholders to coordinate investigations and remedial actions
Develop and refine investigation metrics, dashboards, case studies, and trend analyses to support program improvement and decision-making
Plan, implement, upgrade, and monitor computer network/information security measures and controls.
Serve as ISSO/ISSM for multiple classified information systems, ensuring compliance with applicable government and organizational cyber security requirements.
Identify security needs and develop system security plans; coordinate implementation of security architecture and applications.
Oversee security sustainment activities including account management, media protection, audit logging, and secure file processes
Perform risk assessments, penetration testing, system log analysis, and vulnerability evaluations.
Develop and execute risk remediation plans, recommend security technologies.
Conduct user compliance monitoring and address organizational security deficiencies.
Develop, deliver, and update security awareness training and materials.
Assist with maintaining ongoing security infrastructure, update cyber protection measures, and research or develop incident response tools and processes.
Produce intelligence products (alerts, briefs, reports) that translate complex technical findings into clear, actionable guidance for stakeholders.
Perform proactive threat hunting in classified and unclassified environments to identify anomalous behavior and previously undetected threats.

Education & Experience:

Technical bachelor’s degree and 5 or more years related work experience or a master’s degree with 3 or more years or equivalent work experience.
Proven experience in threat intelligence, insider threat analysis, cyber security, and information security investigations.
Strong analytical skills; ability to review and assess intelligence and monitor indicators of compromise.
Experience with intelligence aggregation tools, vulnerability assessment, and risk remediation.
Proficiency in forensic analysis, log analysis, penetration testing, and malware investigation.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of producing clear investigative and security reports.
Knowledge of security architecture, firewalls, and safeguarding procedures.
Familiarity with incident response and recovery steps for security breaches.
Meticulous attention to detail and strong problem-solving skills, ensuring thorough analysis and effective threat response.
Demonstrated ability to exercise discretion, maintain confidentiality, and handle sensitive information appropriately.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance
Familiarity with scripting or automation (e.g. python, powershell)
Knowledge of RMF and government cybersecurity guidance (e.g., NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, CNSSI 1253), and related authorization frameworks.
Experience or familiarity with common information security tools, such as: EDR, Firewall, SIEM, Email Archiver, SEG, DSP, Forensic Suites, eDiscovery, UBA, MDM, and HW/SW write blockers

Preferred Education and Experience:

Degree in Information Security, Cyber Security, Computer Science, Criminal Justice or related field preferred.
Professional cybersecurity or forensic certification desired (e.g. A+, Security+, CISSP, GCIA, GCFA, GCFE, CFCE, ENCE, or similar)

Description

About Leidos Australia

At Leidos Australia, our work goes beyond a job title. We design, build, operate and support the systems, services and capabilities that help protect and advance the Australian way of life.

Backed by a global organisation of more than 40,000 people, our Australian team of around 2,000 has partnered with government, defence and national security customers for more than 30 years. We deliver mission-critical solutions where reliability, trust and purpose matter.

Benefits

Leidos is a destination for people who want their work to have purpose, their contribution to be recognised, and their career to grow without needing to fit a single mould. Meaningful work is supported by benefits, flexibility and career pathways that help you grow while balancing life outside work. This includes:

Flex Your Way – Tailor work to your life with options including Life Days (up to 12 extra days off per year), part-time arrangements, job sharing, and compressed hours.
Learn Without Limits – Access over 120,000 on-demand courses, alongside technical, project management, leadership, and professional development opportunities.
Work That Makes an Impact – Contribute to nationally significant projects that matter, solve complex challenges, and accelerate your career through unique growth opportunities.
Build Your Future – Whether you're deepening technical expertise or preparing for leadership, we'll invest in your development every step of the way.
And Much More – These are just a few of the ways we invest in our people and help them thrive.

About The Team

You’ll join a team where people work with integrity, inclusion, innovation, agility, collaboration and commitment. In practice, that means sharing ownership, solving complex problems together and staying connected to the customer context, the purpose behind the work and how each role contributes to meaningful outcomes.

The Mission Software Solutions business delivers customised and off-the-shelf software solutions to Defence, Intelligence and other Government sectors. The business also builds capabilities for a wide range of traditional and non-traditional environments, with a strong focus on supporting highly secure, intelligence-led mission outcomes and advancing the technological modernisation of complex Government enterprises.

The Opportunity

Our MSS team is seeking experienced Technical Program Managers to support the growth of our Defence & Intelligence business across Australia, with opportunities available in both Melbourne and Canberra.

As we position for a number of significant Defence & Intelligence programs, we are building a pipeline of program leaders who can bring together people, technology and mission outcomes to deliver complex capabilities across secure Defence and Intelligence environments that support Australia’s national security objectives.

In This Role, You Will

Lead the delivery of complex Defence & Intelligence programs spanning software, cloud, cyber, ICT, data and mission-focused technologies, ensuring outcomes are achieved safely, securely and effectively.
Coordinate multidisciplinary teams across engineering, software development, infrastructure, cyber security, testing and operational stakeholders, aligning delivery activities to customer priorities and mission needs.
Partner closely with Defence, Intelligence & National Security customers, program executives and technical leaders to manage program planning, governance, risk, dependencies and performance across the full delivery lifecycle.
Shape the successful execution of emerging and established Defence & Intelligence programs, helping define delivery strategies, build high-performing teams and achieve long-term customer outcomes.

We are particularly interested in hearing from program leaders with experience in one or more of the following domains:

Defence & Intelligence software systems and mission applications
Intelligence, ISR and targeting systems
Geospatial technologies, remote sensing and data exploitation
Enterprise ICT, cloud, infrastructure and network environments
Cyber security, cyber operations and cyber engineering capabilities

About You

We are looking for people who combine program leadership capability, stakeholder engagement experience and delivery expertise with a passion for achieving outcomes that matter in complex Defence and national security environments.

Essential

You've successfully led complex technical programs or large-scale projects, balancing customer expectations, delivery objectives, risk management and operational outcomes.
You're comfortable working across diverse technical disciplines, bringing together engineers, architects, developers and delivery teams to achieve shared goals.
You know how to build trusted relationships with customers, senior stakeholders and partners, navigating complexity while maintaining focus on mission success.
You bring experience delivering technology-enabled outcomes in one or more areas such as Defence & Intelligence systems, mission software, cyber security, cloud, ICT, data or related domains.
You can establish effective governance, planning and reporting practices, ensuring programs remain aligned to strategic priorities, delivery milestones and customer outcomes.
You are an Australian Citizen who currently holds at least an NV2 Australian Government security clearance and able to obtain and maintain a clearance up to TSPV. Candidates who currently hold an active TSPV security clearance are strongly encouraged to apply.

Advantageous

You've delivered Defence & Intelligence acquisition, systems integration, transition or sustainment programs and understand the challenges of operating within complex customer environments.
You have experience leading programs involving multiple stakeholders, subcontractors or integrated delivery teams across distributed locations.
You bring familiarity with program governance frameworks, commercial management, customer engagement and strategic planning activities.
You understand the security, regulatory and operational considerations associated with delivering solutions for Defence, Intelligence and national security customers.

What To Expect When You Apply

Our hiring process is designed to be straightforward, respectful and easy to navigate. If your skills, experience and qualifications look aligned with the role, our Talent Acquisition team will contact you to discuss the next stage. You can expect:

An initial conversation with our Talent Acquisition team
An interview with the hiring manager or interview panel
Any role-specific assessment, technical discussion or customer step required for the position

We’ll let you know what to expect before each stage, including who you’ll meet and how to prepare. If you need any adjustments or support during the process, please let us know.

Ready to explore what’s possible?

If this sounds like a role where you can make an impact and continue to grow, we’d like to hear from you. Please apply via the “Apply Now” button with your resume. If you have any questions about the role or recruitment process, please contact Cam Larkin, Talent Acquisition – cameron.larkin@au.leidos.com.

If you're looking for comfort, keep scrolling. At Leidos, we outthink, outbuild, and outpace the status quo — because the mission demands it. We're not hiring followers. We're recruiting the ones who disrupt, provoke, and refuse to fail. Step 10 is ancient history. We're already at step 30 — and moving faster than anyone else dares.

Original Posting

For U.S. Positions: While subject to change based on business needs, Leidos reasonably anticipates that this job requisition will remain open for at least 3 days with an anticipated close date of no earlier than 3 days after the original posting date as listed above.

Pay Range

The Leidos pay range for this job level is a general guideline onlyand not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law.

About Leidos

Leidos is an industry and technology leader serving government and commercial customers with smarter, more efficient digital and mission innovations. Headquartered in Reston, Virginia, with 47,000 global employees, Leidos reported annual revenues of approximately $16.7 billion for the fiscal year ended January 3, 2025. For more information, visit www.Leidos.com.

Pay And Benefits

Pay and benefits are fundamental to any career decision. That's why we craft compensation packages that reflect the importance of the work we do for our customers. Employment benefits include competitive compensation, Health and Wellness programs, Income Protection, Paid Leave and Retirement. More details are available at www.leidos.com/careers/pay-benefits.

Securing Your Data

Beware of fake employment opportunities using Leidos’ name. Leidos will never ask you to provide payment-related information during any part of the employment application process (i.e., ask you for money), nor will Leidos ever advance money as part of the hiring process (i.e., send you a check or money order before doing any work). Further, Leidos will only communicate with you through emails that are generated by the Leidos.com automated system – never from free commercial services (e.g., Gmail, Yahoo, Hotmail) or via WhatsApp, Telegram, etc. If you received an email purporting to be from Leidos that asks for payment-related information or any other personal information (e.g., about you or your previous employer), and you are concerned about its legitimacy, please make us aware immediately by emailing us at LeidosCareersFraud@leidos.com.

If you believe you are the victim of a scam, contact your local law enforcement and report the incident to the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.

Commitment to Non-Discrimination

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, ethnicity, age, national origin, citizenship, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy, family structure, marital status, ancestry, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law. Experience managing quoting, pricing validation, approval routing, product configuration, and commercial exceptions.
Hands-on experience with CPQ platforms, preferably DealHub, and CRM systems such as HubSpot or Salesforce.
Strong analytical and financial skills, including deal modeling, KPI reporting, margin analysis, discount governance, and revenue recognition principles.

new_jobs.title: New Games Business Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Help us decide which games are worth building — and how much to invest on the ones that work.

We're looking for a Business Analyst to help decide which new games Wildlife should build, scale, and invest in - and how to do it. You’ll be part of the New Games Product Marketing team at Wildlife Studios.

New Games is where the portfolio of the next few years takes shape. We take concepts — sometimes a single playable ad, sometimes a prototype with a few levels — put them in front of real players and ask: is there a business here, and if so, how do we make it work at scale? That means figuring out not just whether players want the game, but how to find them and acquire them efficiently. You'll work across experimentation, modeling, product analytics, market and distribution strategy, and investment decisions - often with limited data and no obvious right answer. You'll need to understand the product, challenge assumptions, figure out what the data can actually tell us, and turn that into a recommendation: what should we build, who should we build it for, how do we reach those players, and how much should we invest?

We work with games from their earliest concepts, even before a line of code exists, all the way through global launch. Throughout that journey, the work is the same: understand the product deeply, dig into the data, help make it better, and figure out the best way to distribute it.

If you like working in a dynamic place, digging into questions where the data is thin and the answer still matters, and sitting close to product rather than downstream of it, this is the seat.

What You'll Do

Analysis and experimentation: Analyze player and game performance across engagement, monetization, and cost of acquisition, turning data into a clear read and recommendation. Help design and evaluate tests, from concept tests to soft launches, and be clear about what the data can and cannot prove.
Distribution strategy: Help shape how a new game reaches players, including which markets, channels, audiences, and creative angles to test and at what cost. Analyze where investment should go across platforms like Meta, Google, and TikTok, and understand what each platform is actually optimizing
Support kill, iterate, and scale decisions: Build the analysis and recommendations behind key product decisions, bringing a clear view of what the data tells us and what we should do next.
Modeling under uncertainty: Work with early LTV, payback, and market-size models where data is limited. Understand the assumptions behind them and use them to inform investment and growth decisions.
Launch strategy: For the games that graduate, help shape how they go global, including which markets open when, how fast to ramp, and how much to invest.
Problem prioritization: New games generate more questions than we can answer. Use judgment to identify the problems and analyses most likely to change a product or investment decision, and proactively drive them forward.
Cross-functional teamwork: Work alongside the game team, product, and creative across a title's whole life. Bring the market and player read into product discussions, including what players are responding to and what the numbers say the game still has to fix. Bring the product reality back into how the game gets positioned and distributed.

What You'll Need

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Economics, Business, or equivalent practical experience.
Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills — you can explain a model to someone who will never read the code.
Working proficiency in SQL, plus Python or R.
Comfort with incomplete data and questions that arrive badly defined.

Nice to have

Familiarity with A/B testing, multivariate testing, and other methodologies for evaluating performance.
Experience with large datasets, BI tooling, or building data pipelines.
Previous experience in user acquisition, performance marketing, growth, banking, or consulting.
Familiarity with the mobile gaming industry landscape.

More About You

Proactive and autonomous; you drive initiatives without waiting for instructions, while ensuring necessary visibility and buy-in from key stakeholders.
Thrives in high-demand environments and excels at prioritization.
An exceptional communicator who can influence others — including telling a stakeholder their idea won't work, with the data to support it.

About Wildlife

Wildlife is one of the leading mobile game developers and publishers in the world. We have released more than 60 titles, reaching billions of people around the globe. Today, we have offices in Brazil, Argentina, Ireland, and the United States. Here, we create games that will excite, intrigue, and engage our players for years to come!

You'll be joining a friendly and collaborative team where you'll have plenty of opportunity to bring your own ideas, experience and expertise to the role.

As Data & BI Manager, you'll lead and develop our Data Engineering and Business Intelligence teams, including our Data and BI Leads. You'll provide direction and support to help the team deliver great work, while also helping each person develop their skills and progress their career.

You'll have an important role in shaping our data capability, developing standards and ways of working, and helping us continue to improve our approach to data governance, reporting and business intelligence.

You'll also have the opportunity to work with senior stakeholders across the firm, helping them understand what's possible with data and ensuring the information we provide is useful, trusted and easy to understand.

Work closely with Architecture and Delivery colleagues to ensure our data solutions are well designed and fit for purpose.

Work with stakeholders to understand their reporting and data needs and identify opportunities to do things better.
Provide technical oversight of data and BI delivery, ensuring solutions meet agreed standards and business requirements.
Champion the value of data across the firm and help colleagues make better use of the information available to them.

You'll be joining us at an exciting time, with the opportunity to help shape how our data function develops in the future. We're looking for someone who can balance the demands of today with a clear view of where we want to be tomorrow.

We're looking for an experienced data professional who enjoys leading people just as much as they enjoy working with technology.

Strong experience leading and developing data teams, with a genuine interest in coaching and supporting people to reach their potential.

The Ministry of Defence is a central government department with a mission to protect our country and provide the ultimate guarantee of its security and independence, as well as helping to protect its values and interests abroad.

The Directorate for National Security and Global Themes, within MOD Head Office, is responsible for the policy, strategy, planning and governance of strategic operations, special operations, state threats, global issues and cyber. We are a mixed team of military personnel and civil servants, reporting to Director National Security.

This role has a minimum assignment duration of 3 years. An assignment duration is the period of time an employee is expected to remain in the same post to enable them to deliver on the agreed key business outcomes. The assignment duration also supports your career through building your depth of expertise. As part of accepting this role, ideally you will be agreeing to the expected assignment duration set out above. This will not result in a contractual change to your terms and conditions.

This position is advertised at 37 hours per week.

Job Description

The operations overseen by the Directorate are necessarily informed by the advice, insight and understanding of subject matter experts. As a Thematic Research Analyst, you’ll deliver subject matter expertise to decision-makers, so that they can deliver operations that contribute to wider national security goals and priorities. You’ll lead a range of research projects, drawing upon industry, academic and wider HMG expertise to help the Directorate make better decisions. You will have a focus on the pacing threats to national security, and Defence’s role in mitigating them. It’s a fascinating and diverse role where you’ll use everyday skills, including communication and judgement, to tackle extraordinary challenges.

Responsibilities

Successful candidates can expect to be involved in the following:

Collaborating with colleagues and stakeholders across Government to develop insight and understanding to enable decision making.
Building and sustaining relationships with stakeholders, to ensure that the thematic research you conduct is valuable, unique and well-informed.
Bringing together a range of analytical skills to identify problems and find solutions through a multi-disciplinary, collaborative approach.
Providing visible, accessible, and effective subject matter leadership, taking a personal lead in communicating messages with clarity and conviction.
Analysing intelligence and information relating to threats, to continually develop your subject matter expertise and provide timely, robust advice.

You will meet with senior officials and decision-makers to provide up to date and accurate advice. You will work with colleagues across the armed forces, security and intelligence agencies, international allies and partners, industry and academia to deliver real world outcomes. Whatever the requirements, you’ll be at the heart of what we do – contributing to national security and protecting the UK.

To succeed as a Thematic Research Analyst, you’ll need some key attributes. You’ll have first-class interpersonal skills, emotional intelligence and an excellent academic record. You will have a passion for foreign affairs and a keenness to contribute to the UK’s safety and prosperity. You will have evidence from previous roles of taking responsibility and showing clear evidence-based decision making within a national security context; consulting widely and challenging assumptions; as well as using intelligence to enable decisions. You’ll have experience of working with the national security community, ideally in an all-source analytical role.

Responsibilities

Noblis is seeking Identity Intelligence Analyst(s) to work in dynamic mission-oriented environment within McLean, Virginia.
As an Identity Intelligence Analyst, you will analyze and integrate identity intelligence related to terrorism and Counterterrorism (CT), and support CT customers by researching, preparing, and delivering written intelligence products, responses to taskings, and deliver oral presentations.

Job Responsibilities

Conducting identity intelligence analysis to support terrorist nominations, watchlisting, screening, vetting, identity resolution, and counterterrorism operations.
Receiving, reviewing, and processing identity information from classified and unclassified sources in accordance with Intelligence Community policies, standards, and mission requirements.
Evaluating and integrating identity-related intelligence to resolve identities, assess threats, identify associations and patterns, and support adjudication decisions.
Researching and responding to intelligence taskings by developing timely, accurate, and well-supported intelligence products, assessments, and briefings.
Performing quality assurance reviews of intelligence information and products to identify inconsistencies, analytical gaps, and potential issues affecting identity resolution or operational decisions.
Identifying intelligence gaps and conducting targeted research to develop additional information in support of evolving counterterrorism and identity intelligence requirements.
Applying Intelligence Community analytic tradecraft, including ICD 203 and ICD 206, to ensure intelligence products are objective, accurate, properly sourced, and analytically rigorous.
Providing surge support across mission areas and supporting continuous mission operations, including shift-based requirements, to meet evolving operational priorities.

Experience conducting identity intelligence analysis in support of terrorist nominations, watchlisting, screening, and vetting operations by receiving, reviewing, and processing identity information in accordance with Intelligence Community policies and standards.
Experience evaluating and integrating data from classified and unclassified sources to support identity resolution, threat assessments, and adjudication decisions.
Experience performing quality assurance reviews, identifying intelligence gaps and patterns, producing finished intelligence products, and providing surge support across mission areas to meet evolving operational requirements.

new_jobs.title: Senior All-Source Intelligence Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

About The Role

TRM Labs builds the intelligence infrastructure behind the world's most consequential crypto investigations. As a Senior All-source Intelligence Analyst,
you will anchor TRM's in-region targeting capability — working closely with a pod of investigators operating from Southeast Asia to disrupt crypto-enabled scam networks at their source. You will fuse OSINT collection disciplines, in-region operational access, and financial intelligence to build targeting packages on the scam compound operators, financial service providers, and cyber infrastructure that enable large-scale fraud across the region.

The Impact You Will Have

Run intelligence and OSINT operations end-to-end against scam infrastructure across Southeast Asia, converting collection into targeting-ready intelligence for TRM teams and government partners.
Trace scam compounds geographically and operationally — combining cell triangulation, IP geolocation, GEOINT, adtech, physical OSINT, on-chain attribution, and commercially available data to identify operators, controllers, and movement patterns across across Myanmar, Laos, Cambodia, and Thailand.
Work the intelligence flywheel operationally — processing investigative returns at high volume and feeding victim, operator, and infrastructure data into TRM’s intelligence and product pipelines.
Find the seams — pivot from a single victim, wallet, device, or compound lead into uncovering broader operational networks and multiplying investigative leads.
Partner with TRM’s Scams SME team, on-chain analysts, and the DC-based targeting cell to translate regional collection and disruption strategy into targeting packages that support government enforcement actions.

What We're Looking For

US Citizenship required. Bangkok presence or extensive APAC travel required.
5-8+ years of all-source investigative or targeting experience — federal law enforcement (former 1811s — e.g., FBI, HSI, IRS-CI, Secret Service), Intelligence Community all-source analysis, or mission-aligned private sector equivalent
Operational Leadership — Proven experience building targeting packages for intelligence or law enforcement partners and coordinating small analytic teams or investigative pods in a player-coach capacity.
Investigative & Targeting Experience — in the Intelligence Community, DoD, federal law enforcement, or a mission-aligned private sector environment.
OSINT Tradecraft — Hands-on experience with cell triangulation, IP geolocation, GEOINT, AdTech analysis, and infrastructure attribution.
Targeting & Analysis Skills — Proven ability to build operational intelligence products and pivot from a single lead into broader operational networks using strong link and pattern analysis.
APAC Operational Experience — Southeast Asia field experience (particularly Thailand, Myanmar, Laos, or Cambodia) strongly preferred; regional language skills are a major differentiator.
AI & Investigative Fluency — Comfortable using AI tools to accelerate investigative workflows, synthesize data, and draft operational outputs.
Mission Alignment — Financial crime or crypto experience is a plus, not a requirement.

About The Team

TRM's Primary Intelligence function sits within R&D and leads intelligence product development for government and commercial customers
Close collaboration with TRM's Scams SME team, who provide foundational scam compound domain context
This is a build role: you will establish TRM's APAC field presence and targeting capability from the ground up

Team Operating Rhythms

Weekly team syncs to align targeting priorities and review disruption opportunities
Daily async standups via Slack on active work, returns, and target packages in flight
Primary time zone overlap: US Eastern / APAC
All output documented in Notion and TRM’s investigative tools
Surge availability expected during time-sensitive disruption windows

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves quickly. We are a high velocity, high ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, You Should Expect

Priorities and targets to change quickly as we experiment and iterate
Work that often requires operating with a high degree of ambiguity
A high level of personal ownership and accountability
Close collaboration across teams and functions
Frequent, high-touch communication
Creative problem solving and out-of-the-box thinking
A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires comfort navigating ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

At the same time, many people find this work deeply rewarding. If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. Learn more: Interviewing at TRM: How We Hire and What Success Looks Like

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI Fluency Means You Are Among The Top 10 Percent Of Operators In Your Function In How You Apply AI To

Accelerate repeatable workflows
Structure and solve problems
Improve output quality
Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.
Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.
Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

Privacy Policy And Additional Information

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com.

To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates.

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form.

Recruitment agencies

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.
